clue.text: Sauce label put on with name of firm

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another is set beside it to build the word

parts.note: a tab is a small label or tag attached to something
with and as overlap in phrases such as 'as well as', meaning along with
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A brand label is stuck onto a bottle together with the maker's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' joins the pieces in order; 'name of' is a link. The weakest step is 'with' for AS, as in 'as well as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of hot pepper condiment from Louisiana.

clue.text: Their work is somewhat mechanical, but character-forming

definitions.text: Their work is somewhat mechanical, but character-forming

parts.words: Their work is somewhat mechanical, but character-forming
parts.note: sounds like dull jobs that build moral fibre, but keyboard workers form printed letters

explanation.definitionFit: Office workers at keyboards produce letters, the characters of text.

clue.text: Battle helmet

definitions.meaning: the 1854 Crimean engagement of the Charge of the Light Brigade
a knitted hood covering the head and neck

explanation.definitionFit: Balaclava was a Crimean War engagement of 1854; a woollen hood covering head and neck is named after it.

clue.text: Deserted area is in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way suggests the letters of is in a are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An abandoned place has fallen into a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad way' rearranges ISINA. 'in a' looks like part of the phrase 'in a bad way' but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinai peninsula in Egypt is largely desert.

clue.text: A composer frequently, we hear, supported by another

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supported by another sits above it
we hear says a word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: often means frequently
Bach is another composer

explanation.surface: One composer is often backed up by a second.
explanation.walkthrough: OFTEN said with a silent T sounds like OFFEN; 'supported by' puts it above BACH. Jacques Offenbach wrote operettas.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach was a 19th-century French-German writer of operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld.

clue.text: The talk of the district

parts.note: reads as local gossip everyone is discussing, but means the regional form of speech used there

explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of a language is the way people of an area speak.

clue.text: Plant oneself on the end of a bed spring

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of bed

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Sit down on the tail of a mattress coil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 'spring' means a water source, not a coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside or linger somewhere is to settle and stay put.

clue.text: Soldiers in camp — sorry, on manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests movement, so the letters of camp and sorry march into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops in a camp apologise while out on exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' rearranges CAMPSORRY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a large military formation of several divisions of troops.

clue.text: Result of unseen incomplete-result to follow

indicators.note: the result of a word's letters being worked over is a new arrangement
incomplete drops the last letter of unseen

explanation.surface: An unseen outcome is still to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts UNSEEN to UNSEE, which 'Result of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to come after as an effect.

clue.text: A furious pet

parts.note: sounds like an angry animal, but a pet is also a fit of sulking, so this is a furious outburst

explanation.definitionFit: A child's screaming fit of rage is a furious fit of temper.

clue.text: It may hold up current supplies

definitions.text: It may hold up current supplies

parts.words: It may hold up current supplies
parts.note: sounds like a hold-up of present stock, but current is electricity carried on cables a tall steel tower supports

explanation.definitionFit: A tall lattice tower carries overhead power cables across country.

clue.text: Forenames unusual in a lodger

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the previous word come in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Some first names are rare for a person renting a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lodger' is not a tenant but a member of a Masonic lodge; 'unusual' rearranges FORENAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Masonic brotherhood meet in local lodges, so one is a lodge member.

clue.text: Irregular coastline, not all in one piece

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of the next word lose their usual order

explanation.surface: A jagged shoreline is broken into separate bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' rearranges COASTLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made in separate parts that fit together, like a modular sofa, is built in sections.

clue.text: Empty vault

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to remove everything from somewhere
as a verb, to leap over an obstacle

explanation.definitionFit: To empty a room is to remove its contents; to vault a fence is to jump over it without touching.

clue.text: Navigational aids for sailor on ship

indicators.note: a sailor on a ship is aboard it, so the sailor's word sits within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: Equipment supplied to a seaman aboard a vessel to help him find his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means aboard, putting TAR inside SS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors once fixed their position at sea by taking sightings of heavenly bodies.

clue.text: She cleans out for the steward

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of She cleans are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A woman does the cleaning for the household manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SHECLEANS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was the officer in charge of a medieval noble household.

clue.text: In the morning our Bert goes round the botanical park

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: goes round says the letters of our Bert turn about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Each morning a local man named Bert takes a stroll around the public gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' rearranges OURBERT to RBORETU, which 'In' puts inside AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a collection of trees grown for study and display, a kind of botanical garden.

clue.text: China has a poor start to the game

indicators.note: start says the poor word goes at the beginning of the china word

parts.note: bad means poor
Minton is a famous brand of English porcelain

explanation.surface: China has made a weak opening in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Minton is a Staffordshire pottery firm; 'China' suggests the country but is porcelain. 'start' puts BAD before MINTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a net.

clue.text: Well, no one wants it

parts.note: if you are healthy, no medical care is needed

explanation.definitionFit: Medical care is given to the sick, which healthy people never need.

clue.text: Arrested unyielding pressman

parts.note: staunch means loyal and firm, not giving way
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A stubborn journalist has been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrested' means stopped, as in stemming a flow of blood, not taken by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Stemming the flow of blood from a wound is checking or stopping it.

clue.text: A grain's turned into wine

indicators.note: turned into says the letters of A grain's are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the s included as a letter

explanation.surface: A grain of something has become a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned into' rearranges AGRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit.

clue.text: Gambling row

definitions.meaning: short for a sweepstake, a betting pool
to propel a boat with a long oar

explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery where the pot goes to the winners; a long oar used to propel a boat is also given this name.

clue.text: Gradually learns and improves

definitions.meaning: acquires a skill or language bit by bit

explanation.definitionFit: One acquires a skill by absorbing it bit by bit; trade or health gets better when it recovers.

clue.text: They may be held in revulsion

definitions.text: They may be held in revulsion

parts.words: They may be held in revulsion
parts.note: sounds like things regarded with disgust, but people pinch their nostrils shut against a bad smell

explanation.definitionFit: Faced with a foul smell, people pinch their snouts shut.

clue.text: Painfully done

parts.note: done is slang for cheated, so this is being swindled in a way that hurts, as by an insect

explanation.definitionFit: Being swindled out of money, or pricked by a wasp, both smart.

clue.text: One maxicoat of obvious style

indicators.note: style suggests the letters are refashioned into a different form

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A single long coat of an unmistakable fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges I plus MAXICOAT; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something self-evident needs no proof, like a basic truth in mathematics.

clue.text: Confession of folly at get-together

definitions.note: read as a verb phrase, to get together

parts.note: am is what a person admits in I am
an ass is a fool, the embodiment of folly

explanation.surface: Admitting to a silly mistake at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am an ass' would be a confession of folly; 'of' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or collect a store of things is to gather them up.

clue.text: Be sorry for a doctor given the run-around

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: run-around suggests the letters of run are moved about

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Feel sad about a physician being messed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges RUN into URN; 'given the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve over a loss is to feel deep sorrow about it.

clue.text: Disorderly actors are plastered

parts.note: rough means unruly or rowdy
a cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Unruly performers have been drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like drunk; here it means coated with a coarse render of lime and gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse wall render of lime and gravel is applied by plasterers, so such a wall has been coated.

clue.text: Employers requiring faultless service in the US

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the country's letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a vice is a fault, so service without its fault drops those four letters

explanation.surface: Bosses demand impeccable work across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faultless' takes VICE (a fault) from SERVICE to leave SER, which 'in' puts inside US; 'requiring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People who use something employ it, making them its employers in a literal sense.

clue.text: Prayers for one who may supply money to us

parts.note: an angel is a backer who invests in a stage production
taken as written

explanation.surface: People pray for a financial backer to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: An ANGEL is theatre slang for a financial backer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion recited morning, noon and evening, a set of prayers.

clue.text: Without any breaks? That's no French way to work

parts.note: non is French for no
St is short for street, a way
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to work without stopping, the French saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is ST for street and 'work' is OP for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something continuous carries on without pause or interruption.
